question.text: What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
question.explanation:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by \[ \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1. \]

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=4$ and the vertical radius has length $b=7.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is \[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2} &= 1 \\[3pt] \dfrac{x^2}{4^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{7^2} &= 1 \\[3pt] \dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{49} &= 1. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Determining the Equation of a Tall Ellipse

question.text: What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of an ellipse with equation $\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{36} = 1?$
question.explanation:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by \[ \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1. \]

In the given equation, we have $a^2=9$ and $b^2=36.$

  • Since $a^2=9,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{9} = 3.$

  • Since $b^2=36,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{36} = 6.$

Thus, the semi-major axis has length $b=6,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $a=3.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2b = 2 \cdot 6 = 12,$ and the minor axis has length $2a= 2 \cdot 3 =6.$

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=4$ and the vertical radius has length $b=9.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is \[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2} &= 1 \\[3pt] \dfrac{x^2}{4^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{9^2} &= 1 \\[3pt] \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{81}} &= 1. \end{align*} \]
